items.prompt: Why can a comment describing a code block silently become wrong over time?
choices: Comments are automatically deleted by most compilers
Nothing stops the code beneath a comment from changing while the comment itself stays the same, since they're not the same artifact
Comments are only readable by the original author

items.explanation: L2 explains this directly — a comment is a separate translation layer from the code, so nothing enforces that the two stay in sync as the code changes.
items.reference:
Comment: separate from the code, can drift out of sync

Extracted function name: IS the description, can't drift

Why: a function's name and its behavior are the same artifact — a comment and the code it describes are not.
items.learnMore:
Structure that can't lie

An extracted, well-named function can still be wrong, but it can't independently drift out of sync with itself the way a comment can drift out of sync with the code beneath it.

Common mistake

Relying on step-by-step comments to explain a long function instead of extracting the steps into named functions.
